key_insight: D2Skill maintains a dynamic dual-granularity skill bank—task-level skills for high-level guidance and step-level skills for fine-grained corrections—so an agent can reuse and adapt past experience more effectively during RL training.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of principled, evolving skill memory in skill-based RL: existing methods focus on trajectory-level guidance and miss fine-grained, stepwise corrections and continual updating of reusable skills.
method: Dual-granularity skill bank: store and represent reusable experience as task skills (trajectory/plan-level) and step skills (local/action-level) for complementary roles.
Dynamic memory management: jointly train the policy and skill bank with mechanisms to add, update, and prune skills online so the memory evolves with learning.
Skill-conditioned control: retrieve and apply task skills for high-level planning while invoking step skills for fine-grained decision support and error correction during execution.
impact: Enables more sample-efficient, robust, and transferable agentic RL by combining long-horizon guidance with precise corrective actions—beneficial for practitioners building adaptive agents and continual learning systems.
visual_elements: Architectural diagram showing policy interacting with a dual-granularity skill bank (task skills vs step skills) with arrows for retrieval and updates.
Sequence timeline illustrating dynamic skill bank lifecycle: creation, usage, update, and pruning during training.
Bar or line chart comparing sample efficiency / success rate of baseline RL vs D2Skill across tasks.
Flowchart showing decision-time behavior: high-level plan selection via task skills, then step-skill corrections applied to executed actions.
paper_title: Dynamic Dual-Granularity Skill Bank for Agentic RL
paper_authors: Songjun Tu, Chengdong Xu, Qichao Zhang, Yaocheng Zhang, Xiangyuan Lan
